title: paged KV cache: adaptive block allocator + locality-aware pinning heuristic
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Improves KV cache block allocator to adaptively reuse allocations and a locality-aware pinning heuristic. Expect ~10-15% latency reduction on long-sequence workloads and 15-25% throughput improvement for high concurrency scenarios.
body:
Motivation: The paged KV cache has been a major throughput/latency bottleneck in long-context workloads. Static allocator heuristics and coarse pinning lead to unnecessary evictions and cross-GPU scatter for multi-stream workloads. This PR introduces (1) an adaptive block allocator that prefers reuse of recently-freed blocks when access patterns indicate temporal locality, and (2) a locality-aware pinning heuristic that biases pinning toward the GPU/NUMA region where the block was most frequently accessed.

Design summary: - Adaptive allocator: tracks per-block recent access score and time-since-free; when allocating we prefer blocks with high reuse score to reduce fragmentation and re-copy overhead. Includes a small LRU-like fast-path for hot blocks. - Locality-aware pinning: maintain lightweight access counters per block (decayed over time). When pinning, prefer blocks whose hot-region matches the requesting worker; fall back to global pool if no locality matches. - TTL and eviction: tighten TTL decay when reuse drops to avoid holding cold blocks. Add metrics to track reuse hits/misses, pin locality decisions, and eviction reasons.

Results: Microbenchmarks on c5-gpu-large (A100-like) synthetic traces: - Single-stream long context (32k tokens): median latency down 12%, p95 down 9%. - Multi-stream (32 concurrent streams): overall throughput +18%, tail latency improvement ~14%. - Memory footprint: slightly higher transient reuse (due to conservative pinning) but overall reduced re-copy counts by ~28%.

Backward compatibility: All changes are internal to the paged KV cache and allocator interfaces remain stable. Pinning heuristics are configurable via runtime flags and can be disabled for legacy deployments.

Testing: - Unit tests for allocator edge cases, pin/unpin races, and TTL behavior. - Integration tests in perf-canary and benchmark-lab. - Canary rollout across a subset of Dedicated nodes for 48h: no errors, no increased OOMs.

Checklist: - [x] Add allocator + pinning unit tests - [x] Add metrics (reuse_hits, reuse_misses, pin_locality_matches) - [x] Perf benchmarks in benchmark-lab - [x] Docs: config flags and observability notes - [x] Canary: 48h smoke

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the allocator policy conservative to avoid increased fragmentation in pathological workloads. Follow-up work (ENG-1898) will expose an aggressive mode that is safe for single-tenant Dedicated deployments.

review_comments: Daniel Park: Can you explain why we prefer recently-freed blocks versus strict LRU? Concerned about fragmentation in skewed workloads.

Ava Martinez: The allocator scores blocks by (recent_access_score - time_since_free). The prefer-reuse path only wins when score is above threshold; otherwise we fall back to global allocation to avoid fragmentation. Added unit tests that simulate heavy skew.
Maya Singh: We need to ensure pin counters can't overflow under high QPS; add decay and bounds.
Ava Martinez: Added 64-bit counters with periodic exponential decay and explicit saturation protection per review. Also added a metric to track saturation events.
Omar Rahman: CI showed a flake in allocator_tests on first run (race). Is this resolved?
Ava Martinez: Fixed race by moving ownership into a mutex-protected freelist and added deterministic thread scheduling in the test. Rerun CI.
Daniel Park: Approving -- observed perf gains on my local perf harness with legacy models. Good to merge after a short canary.
Maya Singh: Approving -- config flags look good and documented.
ci_checks: perf-regression-check: pass (benchmarked against baseline, see bench link)
performance_summary: Adaptive allocator + locality pinning reduced re-copy events by ~28% on synthetic traces. Median latency improvements around 10-12% on long-context workloads and throughput improvements of 15-20% under high concurrency. Metrics instrumented to track regressions.
notes: Flags available: --kv.alloc.adaptive_enable, --kv.pin.locality_window_ms, --kv.alloc.reuse_score_threshold. Aggressive reuse mode planned as follow-up (ENG-1898).
